summary: Every dimension's world border is operating independently, and doesn't appear where it actually is
description:
## The bug

Every dimension's world border is operating independently. Changing the world border in one dimension doesn't effect the other dimensions, and in the case of the Nether and End, won't visually change location even though it has.

## How to reproduce

 - Go into creative mode and do this command in the overworld:

/worldborder set 1000

 - Go to the Nether and /tp to the world border there:

/tp @s 0 50 500

 - Do this command while in the Nether:

/worldborder set 10

It looks as though the world border hasn't moved at all.

/worldborder get

and see that it says the border is 10 blocks, even though you can see otherwise. It looks like the original 1000-block length border.

 - Stay within the bounds of the world border you see and put yourself in survival. You will die. The world border you saw wasn't the world border, it really did move to 10 blocks wide.

 - Go back into creative mode and re-enter the nether, this time teleport to the world border's centre.

/tp @s 0 50 0

 - Go into survival and walk around. The actual world border is invisible, but it's still at 10 blocks wide. You'll experience an invisible force hindering your walk.

 - Return to the overworld and do the /worldborder get command again. Now it tells you it's 1000 blocks, which it is... for that dimension.

 - Repeat for the End, but use a number other than 10 to ensure that the Nether world border and the End world border are operating separately from each other as well as the overworld's.

If you do the /worldborder get command in all three dimensions, you will get three different answers... and the Nether and End's world borders will not be where they look like they are. They will look like they have the same border as the overworld.

 - Repeat the process, changing world border centres instead of size. Changing the worldborder's centre in the Nether won't be the coordinates you put in, they'll be divided by 8. All three dimensions can have different world border centres as they are all operating independently.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create or open a world and enter the Overworld in Creative mode.
2. Set the Overworld world border with `/worldborder set 1000`.
3. Enter the Nether and teleport to `0 50 500` with `/tp @s 0 50 500`.
4. Set the Nether world border with `/worldborder set 10`.
5. Run `/worldborder get` in the Nether and observe that it reports a border size of 10 blocks while the visible border still appears to have the original 1000-block size.
6. Switch to Survival mode.
7. Stay within the bounds of the visible border and observe that the player dies, showing that the actual border has moved to 10 blocks.
8. Switch back to Creative mode.
9. Teleport to the Nether border's center with `/tp @s 0 50 0`.
10. Switch to Survival mode and walk around; observe that the actual 10-block border is invisible and an invisible force hinders movement.

Observed Behavior:
## Actual behavior

The world border state is not synchronized consistently between dimensions:

- Changing the border size in one dimension does not update the border size reported by `/worldborder get` in the other dimensions.
- For example, after setting the Overworld border to `1000` blocks, setting the Nether border to `10` blocks causes `/worldborder get` in the Nether to report `10`, while the visible border still appears to be approximately the size and location of the former `1000`-block border.
- The border’s gameplay restrictions use the newly configured value even when its visual rendering does not. A player can therefore appear to be inside the visible border but still be pushed back or killed by the actual smaller border. Conversely, the border can become invisible after teleporting near its actual center while continuing to restrict player movement.
- The Overworld, Nether, and End can each report different border sizes and centers, indicating that their border states are being handled independently.
- Changing the border center in the Nether also produces an incorrect coordinate: the configured center is divided by eight rather than being applied at the coordinates supplied to `/worldborder center`.

As a result, the border rendered to the player in the Nether and End can show the wrong size or position, while collision and damage checks use a different border state.
Expected Behavior: The world border should be shared consistently across the Overworld, Nether, and End. Changing its size or center in any dimension should update the border in all dimensions, with `/worldborder get` reporting the same values everywhere. The displayed border should match its actual location and enforcement, so players encounter the visible boundary rather than an invisible or misleading one.
